A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study with 22 readable pages, including Appendices A-H. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons locate the changes in Figure 1(b) and the arXiv version/date stamp; pages 3-22 are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original contextual-entrainment experiments, attention-head removal results, and supplementary evaluations of stability, factual recall, in-context learning, and MMLU performance.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices and reports a replacement illustrative result in Figure 1(b).

M1.justification: The differentiable masking procedure, Gumbel-sigmoid estimator, loss function, and removal of entrainment heads are unchanged.

E1.justification: The LRE relations, Brown-corpus random tokens, arithmetic, spelling correction, English-French translation, and MMLU coverage are retained. Figure 1(b)'s replacement remains a related-context geography example.

E2.justification: The original-model, no-context, and head-removal comparison configurations are retained. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Figure 1(b)'s illustrative test context changes from 'Iraq is located on the continent of Asia' to 'Japan is in Asia,' retaining Llama-3.1-8B and the Greece-continent query. The broader evaluation procedures, splits, metrics, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The introductory related-context case in Figure 1(b) is replaced with a different prompt and its output distribution. Head-removal ablations and supplementary stability, cross-relation, and capability analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Paired t-tests and the five-run Jaccard-overlap analysis in Appendix D are retained without changes to run counts or statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 1(b) changes from an Iraq-context result ranking Asia above Europe to a Japan-context result ranking Europe above Asia. These are replacement results under different prompts, not a same-setting performance improvement. All other reported results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(3), the masking and objective definitions, residual-stream formulation, and Jaccard-overlap reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about contextual entrainment, semantic modulation, and suppression through entrainment heads.

C2.justification: Mechanistic explanations, semantic interpretations, and stated limitations are unchanged. Figure 1(b)'s revised caption describes its replacement outcome using the existing interpretation of distraction through increased token probability.

D1.justification: Implementation and hyperparameter disclosures, appendix data-generation instructions and examples, and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to induction heads, knowledge conflicts, and prior distraction research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 1(b)'s subcaption is rewritten from possible incorrect responses to increased distractor probability, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1(b) has a revised bar chart, token ordering, horizontal-axis ticks, displayed prompt, and subcaption. The other panels, figures, tables, and surrounding layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The replacement context in Figure 1(b) no longer repeats the query's phrase 'is located on the continent of,' making it a clearer illustration of the introduction's distinction from copying triggered by a repeated prefix. The caption appropriately describes increased distractor probability while Europe remains first. This is a limited explanatory improvement; the methods, aggregate evidence, and appendices are unchanged.
